title: Planner tool stack: firecrawl-cli, icm-architect, FreeConvert
source: The owner's message of 2026-10-12. Dossiers made by `python -m faceless intake` (GitHub's API answered 403 for icm-architect, so facts come from raw files); FreeConvert read with Exa. Nothing was installed or run: the `npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser` line was read, not executed.

items.name: firecrawl-cli (npm)
items.why: Three HIGH flags (install hook, pipe-to-shell in its docs, asks for secrets) and the exact line the owner pasted, `init --all --browser`, installs skills into every detected coding agent globally and opens a browser login: that rewrites the agent environment, which intake rule 1 forbids and nothing about the planner needs. We already hold FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, so a scrape or search is one reviewed REST call from our own provider code if research ever needs it. Not needed for artwork, lessons or the PDFs.
items.steal: Call Firecrawl's REST API directly from faceless/providers behind a cap when a research brief needs a page read; never run init.
items.owner: Say whether the Firecrawl key should be used for research briefs; do not run `init --all` on any machine that holds other agents' skills.

items.name: icm-architect (RinDig, MIT)
items.why: A Claude skill that scaffolds 'folder structure as agent architecture'. This studio already works that way (CLAUDE.md routes, a CONTEXT.md per workspace, the filesystem is the state). Installing it adds nothing; reading it did: its ten invariants match ours and name two gaps worth closing.
items.steal: Each stage folder's CONTEXT.md states inputs, process, outputs and what a human checks before the next stage; keep reference material apart from per-run products; generated indexes are rebuilt by script, never hand-edited (the planner's INVENTORY.md already is).

web.name: FreeConvert (freeconvert.com, API v1)
web.why: A hosted file-conversion API (convert, compress, resize 200+ formats; job of import, convert, export/url). It has no watermark or handle removal, so it is not the cleaner: that stays local (OpenCV). Its real use here is turning picture formats Pillow cannot open (HEIC, TIFF, PSD, AVIF) into PNG before ingest. Free accounts get 20 conversion minutes a day, 5 minutes per file, API use needs a free account token; files are uploaded to FreeConvert and deleted after a few hours. Written as an optional provider, off until the owner creates the token and sets FREECONVERT_API_KEY; never used for anything that must stay private.
web.steal: The job shape (import, convert, export/url, poll) and per-task refunds on failure.
web.owner: Create a free FreeConvert account and put the API token in the environment as FREECONVERT_API_KEY (intake never signs up for anyone).

web.name: Photopea (photopea.com, live-messaging API)
web.why: The owner's own cropper. Photopea runs in the browser on our machine (its docs say files are not uploaded; the editor's code and ads load from photopea.com) and has an official, free messaging API: send the picture, run `app.activeDocument.crop([l,t,r,b])`, `saveToOE`. Driven headlessly in the pre-installed Chromium through Playwright (Apache-2.0, USE 2026-10-11). Measured: starts in about 3 s, a crop takes under a second, and every result is checked against a plain Pillow crop; Pillow is the fallback if the site is slow or blocked. Used on 14 of the owner's 44 wellness posters.
web.steal: Its scripting API (crop, resize, layers, export) for any later batch edit the owner would do by hand.

web.name: Jev 1.13 on OpenRouter (typesafe/jev-1.13, Decisions API)
web.why: The decision surface is OpenRouter's Decisions API (POST /api/alpha/decisions), not the chat router: question types are choice, noul (yes/no probability) and score, and the answer carries calibrated probabilities. It runs on the existing OPENROUTER_API_KEY (no TypeSafe key needed), costs a fraction of a cent and is capped by [decide] decisions_daily_usd. USE as the typed-question gate (decide backend openrouter-decisions; the old jev-openrouter alias maps to it). The chat router typesafe/jev-router is not a decision model; it stays a locator candidate only (9 of 15 handles on the 44 posters against Haiku 5.5's 15 of 15).
web.steal: Ask every gate as typed questions and act on the probability: defer to a person when it is low.

web.name: Microsoft-Decision-1 on OpenRouter (microsoft/microsoft-decision-1)
web.why: A small Azure decision model (ctx 32768, $0.042 per million input tokens) that returns a calibrated probability for each fixed answer instead of text, so the answer carries its own confidence and the app can act, defer or ask for review. Same Decisions API and the same cap as Jev. Used in the product-structure panel (picked C at 0.86 but rated a third listing justified at only 0.07, which the coherence check overruled) and available as a gate backend.
web.steal: Use the confidence to route: act above a high bar, ask a person below it.
